title: Load transient: 1mA <-> 50mA step response
claim: Substantiates spec/target-spec.md's ratified "Load transient" row (1<->50 mA step, ~1us edges: peak excursion <=150mV, recover to +-1% in <=20us, over the ratified C_out/ESR window) against the LDO core-regulation-loop schematic landed by #14 (design/ldo_3v3in_1v8out.sch). Both the spec row and the C_out/ESR window (spec/decision-records/DR-002) are ratified by issue #1 / DR-006, and the bounds below cite those numbers verbatim, not an invented final limit. This testbench's undershoot/overshoot measurements are computed as the deviation from the pre-step (light-load) steady-state value, not an absolute vout bound. Issue #180 brought this bench into conformance with sim/README.md's "Initial-condition contract (issue #171)": the transient is released from an eleven-node `.ic`-constrained operating point (#164's variant-B shape, PR #170 -- see testbench/tb_load_transient.sch's header and this manifest's deck.analyses comments) instead of from ngspice's own unconstrained loop-closed `.op`, which 23 of the 45 corner logs in the superseded 20260825-081255-4cb27f8 record show hitting a singular-matrix / gmin-stepping diagnostic. The stimulus, the step timestamps, the C_out/ESR point and every measurement bound are unchanged by that conversion; the pre-step reference moved from v(vout)[0] to a 0.800-0.999ms average and the peak searches were windowed to the stepped region, because under an `.ic` seed t=0 is the seed itself rather than the corner's own settled 1mA point. The row has TWO independent clauses and, until #119, this manifest measured only the first: undershoot_v/overshoot_v cover "peak excursion <=150mV", and recovery_rise_us/recovery_fall_us (added in #119) cover "recover to +-1% in <=20us" on the rising and falling load edges respectively. Both clause bounds are quoted verbatim from the same ratified row. Issue #119 also moved C_out from the superseded record's 1uF (DR-002's recommended nominal) to 4.7uF (DR-002's ratified window's own ceiling, still 0-500mOhm ESR -- not a value outside the ratified window) to address the peak-excursion clause, which #119 root-caused as charge-limited (Q=C*dV against the loop's finite large-signal response time, not phase-margin-limited -- see design/README.md's #115 anti-correlation finding). C_out/ESR remain a single representative point inside the ratified window, not a sweep of the window -- walking the window inside one deck the way sim/loop-gain does is still follow-on scope (e.g. #19). See spec/decision-records/DR-002's append and design/README.md's "#119" section for the full per-corner evidence, including the recovery-time clause's own, opposite-direction relationship to C_out (this record's own #119 writeup) that this C_out choice does not close. Known-immature-design caveat (design/README.md "Known gaps"): C_COMP/C_CL remain unsized placeholders and the error amplifier still has a light-load/high-VIN output-swing ceiling (design/README.md's "Known open item") even though issue #22 already added the current-limit and soft-start protection circuitry, so a FAIL here -- especially at the high-VIN corner -- is an honest, expected finding at this design stage (per CLAUDE.md's "Verification is the product"), not a harness defect.
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix check, not a distribution claim)

analyses: * --- initial-condition contract (issue #171), applied by issue #180 ---
* This `tran` deliberately carries NO `uic`: the transient is released from
* an operating-point solve that testbench/tb_load_transient.sch's IC_SEED
* `.ic` card constrains to the loop's intended regulating branch at the
* pre-step 1 mA load. That is #164's variant-B shape (PR #170), the second of
* the two shapes sim/README.md's "Initial-condition contract (issue #171)"
* accepts, and the shape sim/ic-screen-125c-b uses. It was chosen over `uic`
* + an EN-edge preamble because this bench steps the LOAD at an already-
* regulating condition: an EN preamble would shift every timestamp below AND
* make C_OUT's pre-step charge state depend on the soft-start ramp, which
* #119's charge-limited peak-excursion finding (see this manifest's claim)
* requires be held fixed. The step edges (1.000ms / 2.001ms) and the 3ms span
* are therefore unchanged from the superseded 20260825-081255-4cb27f8 record.
tran 200n 3m
* --- reference levels ---
* The pre-step steady state is sampled as an average over the last 200us
* BEFORE the rising load edge rather than as v(vout)[0]. Under the `.ic` seed
* t=0 is the seed itself (VOUT clamped to 1.8 exactly), not this corner's own
* settled 1mA operating point, so v(vout)[0] is no longer the right reference;
* 0.800m-0.999m is long after the seed has relaxed and entirely before the step.
* v_post_min / v_post_max are likewise windowed to the stepped region (from
* the rising edge on) so the seed's own relaxation transient cannot be read as
* a load-step excursion. Both windows end at 2.999m, matching w_fall below.
meas tran v_pre AVG v(vout) FROM=0.800m TO=0.999m
meas tran v_post_min MIN v(vout) FROM=1.000m TO=2.999m
meas tran v_post_max MAX v(vout) FROM=1.000m TO=2.999m
meas tran v_50ma FIND v(vout) AT=2.000m
* --- helper vectors for the row's SECOND clause: recover to +-1% in <=20us ---
* The load step is PULSE(1m 50m 1m 1u 1u 1m 4m): the rising edge starts at
* TD = 1.000ms and the falling edge at TD+TR+PW = 2.001ms. Recovery time is
* the last instant, inside the window that follows an edge, at which |vout -
* pre-step vout| still exceeds 1% of the pre-step value -- i.e. the time at
* which the output has re-entered the +-1% band and stays there.
* 'outband' / 'w_*' are 0/1 indicator vectors built arithmetically
* (0.5*(1+x/|x|)) rather than with the comparison operators: ngspice's
* .control parser reads a bare '<' or '>' as an I/O redirection, so
* '(time > 1.0m)' does not survive into the deck.
let vpre = v_pre
let dev = abs(v(vout) - vpre)
let band = 0.01 * vpre
let outband = 0.5*(1 + (dev-band)/(abs(dev-band)+1e-18))

measurements.name: undershoot_v
measurements.note: Worst-case dip below the pre-step (light-load, ~1mA) steady-state value, across the stepped region of the transient (t=1.000m..2.999m, i.e. from the rising load edge to the end of the run). Ratified bound: spec/target-spec.md "Load transient" row, peak excursion <=150mV (ratified by issue #1 / DR-006). Issue #180 re-expressed this from `v(vout)[0] - vecmin(v(vout))` when the deck adopted #171's initial-condition contract: under the `.ic` seed t=0 is the seed value, not this corner's settled 1mA point, and the seed's own relaxation before the step is not a load-step excursion. Neither the quantity nor the bound changed -- only the reference sample and the search window.

measurements.name: overshoot_v
measurements.note: Worst-case rise above the pre-step steady-state value (captures ringing on the 50mA->1mA recovery edge), over the same t=1.000m..2.999m stepped window as undershoot_v. Same ratified 150mV bound as undershoot_v, and re-expressed by #180 for the same reason (see undershoot_v's note).

measurements.name: recovery_rise_us
measurements.note: Recovery time on the 1mA->50mA edge: microseconds from the start of the rising load edge (t=1.000ms) until v(vout) is back inside +-1% of the pre-step value and stays there. Ratified bound: spec/target-spec.md "Load transient" row, "recover to +-1% in <=20us" (ratified by issue #1 / DR-006). Added in #119 -- the row has always had two clauses and until now the harness measured only the peak-excursion one. Read with settle_err_50ma_pct: if that diagnostic is itself outside +-1%, this corner's rising-edge recovery is bounded by steady-state load regulation (the sim/load-regulation row, #118), not by transient settling.

measurements.name: recovery_fall_us
measurements.note: Recovery time on the 50mA->1mA edge: microseconds from the start of the falling load edge (t=2.001ms, i.e. TD+TR+PW of the PULSE source) until v(vout) is back inside +-1% of the pre-step value and stays there. Same ratified 20us bound as recovery_rise_us. This edge is the harder one by construction: the pass device can only source current, so the excess charge the overshoot leaves on C_out can only be removed by the light load itself, which floors this measurement at C_out*(overshoot_v - 0.01*vout)/I_light regardless of the loop.

measurements.name: settle_err_50ma_pct
measurements.note: DIAGNOSTIC, no bound -- not a spec claim. Steady-state output error at 50mA (sampled 1ms after the rising edge, just before the falling edge) relative to the pre-step 1mA value (v_pre, the 0.800m-0.999m average), in percent. Present so recovery_rise_us can be read unambiguously: a corner whose 50mA steady state is already outside the +-1% band can never clear recovery_rise_us no matter how fast the loop settles, and that is a DC load-regulation shortfall (sim/load-regulation, #118) surfacing here rather than a transient one.
